notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Jefferson County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $5,882,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts cash contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for mayor and city council who filed with the NADC since 2023. Candidates file with the NADC once they raise or spend more than $5,000, so smaller races are not included. The NADC files nonprofits with businesses, so both are counted as business money. Individuals, candidates' own money, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Fairbury's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Nebraska yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
